binomial.note: no trials at all: 1.0, because no evidence is not evidence of no difference
no trials, and a wins count that cannot have happened: still 1.0, the guard runs first
one trial, lost: the whole distribution is no more likely than observed
one trial, won: mirror of the above, and 1.0 for the same reason
every pair one way, small: 2/1024 by hand
every pair the other way: identical p by symmetry
every pair one way, long enough that the exact side's coefficient is large
a shutout over a real A/B's pair count - deep underflow, ~1e-79
the smallest possible tie
dead even: every outcome is no more likely than the mode, so exactly 1.0
dead even, odd-sized tail on each side
odd trials, so there is no single mode and the two central outcomes tie
one pair off dead even: the symmetric partner must be counted in
the mirror of the above, which must return the identical p
one off even again, at a different parity
lopsided: the tail the harness reports as significant
far tail, low side
the mirror far tail, high side
#115's shape of result: a decisive A/B at a realistic pair count
a modest edge over the same pair count - the marginal call the harness is for
odd trials at a realistic pair count: 130 and 131 tie for the mode, so this is 1.0 and not a near-miss
1000 trials: comb(1000,500) is 2.7e299, just inside the exact side's overflow
1000 trials, slightly off centre - a wide inclusion set in the large regime
1000 trials, one short of a shutout: the narrowest inclusion set at this size
p matches the observed rate exactly: 1.0, and no symmetry to lean on
just off an asymmetric null - genuine near-ties, not exact ones
the other side of the same asymmetric null, which is NOT its mirror
a quarter-null, upper tail
a quarter-null, lower tail
a three-quarter null, far lower tail
small trials, awkward p: the regime where an inclusion set is easiest to get wrong

wilson.note: no trials: [0, 1], the interval that supports no claim
no trials with a nonzero wins count: the guard still runs first
a single loss - the lower clamp's natural home
a single win - and the upper clamp's
no wins over a short run: lower end pinned at 0 by the clamp
all wins over a short run: upper end pinned at 1
one win: asymmetric interval, well inside both clamps
the small even split, where the interval is at its widest
the even split at a hundred
#115's shape of result at its real pair count
one pair off even at a real pair count
a long run: the z^2/(4n^2) term is where a port's operator order shows
a long run near the top, still short of the clamp
z = 1: the continuity term and the denominator both change scale
z for 99%: a wider interval that reaches a clamp the 95% one does not
z = 0: the interval collapses to the point estimate, both clamps inert
a z nobody would use, chosen so both clamps fire at once

bootstrap.note: no values: (0, 0), an interval that brackets zero and claims nothing
one value: the point itself, and no resampling happens
one negative value: the n == 1 branch must not lose the sign
signed margins, the shape the statistic is actually applied to; indices 1 and last
the same sample and the same draws at alpha=0.5, so both indices land mid-array
the same again at alpha=0, the only case that reaches the min(iters-1, ...) clamp
a wholly positive sample: the interval that excludes zero and calls a real difference
noise around zero: the interval that must *not* exclude it
powers of ten, so every distinct resample gives a distinct mean: the one case where an off-by-one at either percentile index cannot hide in a tie
a constant sample: every resample mean is identical and the interval has no width
